name: Alicon Castalloy Ltd
title: Alicon Castalloy Ltd - 531147 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 revenue ₹495 crore (+16% YoY) but gross margin fell to 45% (−248 bps) and PAT ₹24 crore for FY26 vs ₹46 crore; FY27 guided to 8–10% growth ex-aluminium with capex ₹130–150 crore, utilisation ~78%.

summary.headline: Alicon Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record ₹495 crore (+16% YoY), but gross margin fell to 45% and FY27 guidance is 8–10% growth ex-aluminium.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue reached ₹495 crore, up 16% YoY and the highest quarterly figure ever, helped by pass-through aluminium prices and domestic auto demand. Gross margin fell 248 bps YoY to 45% and EBITDA declined 3% YoY to ₹46 crore on aluminium costs and about ₹15 crore of one-time and provision costs. FY26 consolidated income was about ₹1,784 crore (+4%), EBITDA about ₹203 crore (+3%), and PAT about ₹24 crore versus ₹46 crore, after ₹8 crore of labour-code and exceptional charges. New CEO Sumit Bhatnagar (effective 1 April 2026) set a "Refocus, Reset and Rebuild" theme, with at least one new factory planned in FY27.

segments.name: Domestic automotive
segments.commentary: Principal growth driver in Q4. Two-wheelers ~42% of FY26 business, passenger vehicles ~34%, commercial vehicles ~17–18%, non-auto ~5–6%, per management. Management says CV volumes grew ~19.5% YoY in Q4.

segments.name: International / exports
segments.commentary: Weighed by customer-specific issues and softer export demand; management says deemed exports are about 20% of business. JLR Range Rover programme delayed about 18 months at customer end, now in production with supplies started.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 8–10%, excluding any aluminium price impact; management says aluminium upside is not included.
EBITDA margin expected to rise about 1–1.5 percentage points for the year, to roughly 12.5–13% per CFO, versus about 11.4% in FY26 (CFO clarified this is on an underlying basis).

Management says margins could face pressure in FY27 from input inflation and timing lags, and a Haryana minimum-wage hike is expected to raise labour cost at the Binola plant by about 35% from 1 April 2026.
FY27 capex guided at ₹130–150 crore; about ₹50 crore maintenance and the balance for new projects and expansion, funded through internal accruals.
At least one new manufacturing factory planned in FY27, with the site already finalised.
Management says it will not commit to a precise margin figure while macro volatility persists, and expects more clarity later in the year.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex ₹130–150 crore, focused on die-casting capacity, machining, automation, cybersecurity and a new plant.
Capacity is a constraint: management says new customers face capacity limits, so the new plant is the first step to lift topline.
Asset turnover is below 2x on existing assets; new complex parts need new machining and automation investment. New business target is 2.5–3x asset turnover.
Over 50% of power requirement now met by renewables, mainly solar. Gas use reduced through process changes and some shift to electric heating.
Plant utilisation at about 78%, per an analyst question; management did not dispute this.
demand_pricing: Aluminium prices rose sharply from mid-March 2026 on Middle East tensions; the CFO says prices rose a further ~15–20% in April and rose again in May. Q4 raw-material impact was about ₹30–35 crore QoQ.
Aluminium pass-through is now monthly for most customers, so the CFO says there will be no loss, but no material benefit.
Order wins in FY26: about 14 parts from seven customers, including Audi and Lamborghini for the European location; peak annual sales about ₹140 crore, ₹500–600 crore over 3–4 years.
Daimler CV order: 18 parts, 60% PPAP cleared; peak annual sales ₹80–90 crore, expected at peak in H2 FY28.
New wins: premium 2-wheeler part for higher-CC motorcycles; a turbo core compressor component for data centres (non-auto); an e-Axle housing programme from a German premium OEM.
Order book cut for dropped programs: two large global and two Indian customers removed as volumes did not materialise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue target and medium-term potential, given the ₹7,600 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO guided to 8–10% growth ex-aluminium, calling FY27 a year to refocus, reset and rebuild. Management flagged forward integration and a stronger European base as longer-term moves, without giving numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Were there one-off costs in Q4 and what is the FY27 margin and capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed about ₹30–35 crore of Q4 margin hit to aluminium and about ₹15 crore to one-time costs and provisions. Full-year one-time costs were about ₹25–26 crore. FY27 capex guided at ₹130–150 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What went wrong over the last couple of years, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO cited the JLR Range Rover programme delayed about 18 months at the customer and weak European and US export pull, amid tariffs. Response is to win Indian OEM business and build a new factory; the results are delayed rather than failed.

qa_highlights.question: Is market share being lost domestically, and what was the FY26 domestic and export growth?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO says market share held in models supplied, 2-wheeler share rose, and PV growth lags because Alicon is in fewer models. CFO gave segment mix only; no export growth figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Does the ₹7,600 crore order book (six years) imply a near doubling of revenue, and does it include JLR?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the order book is cumulative FY26–FY31 and implied ~₹3,000–3,500 crore annual run-rate on existing orders. JLR is included, but the CEO declined to disclose the JLR order value, citing contract confidentiality.

qa_highlights.question: Why was ₹25 crore of one-time items not used to lift margin, and what is the margin target?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said margin is a focus but declined to commit to 13–13.5% EBITDA given macro volatility. CFO later pointed to about 12.5–13% for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex be debt-funded, and is the creditor period rising?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said capex will be funded through internal accruals. Creditor days rose to about 135 days in FY26 on vendor-financing arrangements with some customers; most vendors are on 90+ day terms.

risks_watch: Aluminium pass-through timing: pricing is now monthly, but the CFO flagged a further 15–20% rise in April and more in May, so Q1 FY27 margins could be squeezed.
Labour-cost step-up: Haryana minimum-wage increase expected to raise Binola plant labour cost ~35%, with similar moves possible in other states.
Execution risk on new plant and capex, with FY27 targets dependent on capacity coming on stream; management said steep growth will show only towards the end of FY27.
Creditor days rose from about 100 to 135 days in FY26, which could weigh on working capital.
Export weakness in Europe and the US (tariffs, customer-specific issues), with JLR ramp-up timing dependent on the customer.
Order-book quality: a six-year cumulative figure with programme removals and revalidation; no-new-order revenue visibility is less certain than the headline implies.
Management said it would not take conservative targets but declined to commit to specific margins, so guidance credibility is open.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term margins and FY27 growth, citing aluminium, energy and labour cost volatility. Confident on long-term order momentum and domestic demand. The CEO was candid about past execution misses (JLR delay, export underperformance) but gave few hard numbers beyond the 8–10% growth and 12.5–13% margin guidance.
key_quotes: So, this is a year for Alicon to Refocus, Reset and Rebuild.
We will not take any conservative targets for the organization. We will take it very aggressive and we will see.
At this moment, it has to be funded through the internal accruals.
